title: MAS-Attention: Memory-Aware Stream Processing for Attention Acceleration on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices
problem: On resource-constrained edge neural accelerators (e.g., smartphone NPUs), attention acceleration methods like FLAT execute MatMul and softmax sequentially on separate MAC and VEC compute units, leaving one unit idle at all times and achieving suboptimal latency.
motivation: Edge devices have heterogeneous MAC and VEC units that run independently; parallelizing tiled MatMul (on MAC) and softmax (on VEC) exploits this heterogeneity, but requires careful tiling, dependency management, and cache overflow prevention.
method: The approach breaks attention computation into small tiles and runs two separate processing streams in parallel: matrix multiplication (MatMul) on the multiply-accumulate (MAC) units and softmax (the normalization step) on the vector (VEC) units. Instead of running one after the other—which leaves one unit idle—these streams run overlapped in a semi-synchronized pipeline to keep both compute units busy simultaneously. The tile sizes (sub-matrices for MatMul and row-level chunks for softmax) are optimized offline using MCTS (Monte-Carlo Tree Search) and Genetic Algorithm to find the best configuration for the device. To prevent running out of on-chip memory during processing, the system proactively overwrites and reloads intermediate matrices (the K and V tiles) as needed, prioritizing softmax completion to avoid stalling the pipeline.
key_novelty: It's the first attention acceleration method to exploit edge devices' separate compute units (MAC and VEC) by running matrix multiplication and softmax in parallel semi-synchronized pipelines, combined with a proactive strategy that overwrites intermediate data to prevent cache overflow without stalling either stream.
contributions: Semi-synchronous MAC-VEC stream processing scheme parallelizing MatMul and softmax in attention
Multi-tiered tiling scheme with MCTS+GA offline search for optimal tile parameters
Proactive buffer overwrite strategy for cache management under limited on-chip memory
Up to 2.75x speedup and 54% energy reduction vs FLAT (simulated); 1.76x speedup on real Huawei DaVinci NPU

metrics.speedup: Up to 2.75x over FLAT (simulated edge, geomean 1.70x); up to 1.76x on real Huawei MatePad Pro 13.2 DaVinci NPU (geomean 1.42x vs FLAT); 8.50x over Layer-Wise baseline
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 54% energy reduction vs FLAT (simulated); geomean 18.55% energy savings vs FLAT across all networks
metrics.accuracy: Exact attention (golden data validation on all workloads)
metrics.other: Evaluated on BERT, LLaMA3-8B, T5, ViT, XLM; 6% end-to-end latency reduction on Stable Diffusion 1.5 UNet

limitations: Proactive overwrite may increase DRAM reads in some cases, partially negating energy savings; search overhead (MCTS+GA) is significant offline; evaluated only on single-inference scenarios, not batched inference.
